description: Keep a pool of the 5 best packings and, 70% of the time once the pool has 2, start SLSQP from a vertical-cut crossover of two pool members, fixed to 32 circles by random removal or addition.
Run short SLSQP (maxiter 60) restarts for 50% of the time, then polish the top 3 pool packings with maxiter 400.
Screen each SLSQP start with 40 iterations and continue to 300 only if its radius sum is within 3% of the best screening value so far.

After the restart loop, polish the best packing with SLSQP (ftol 1e-14, 500 iterations) in the last 20% of time, repair it, and keep it if the radius sum improves.

issues: No sign of gaming the measurement. There is no file or network access and no pasted coordinates. Randomness comes only from the seeded rng (rng.random and rng.uniform). The ring of 14 circles along the border is a generic starting layout, not a known packing.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. SLSQP still optimises from this start, and the repair step still makes the packing valid. The four side branches of the ring are geometrically consistent.

Possible quality problem, not a reason to veto: the start is built as an (n,2) array and flattened with ravel, so x and y alternate per circle. If _solve_once reads the 2n coordinates as all x values followed by all y values, the ring layout gets scrambled. Check how the start vector is unpacked.
Minor: INIT_LOW and INIT_RADIUS may now be unused in this path, and the fixed values 0.07, 0.93 and 14 are hard-coded. That adds clutter for a change that did not improve the score.

The numbers are consistent. The candidate's loss of -2.9300 is 0.0034 worse than the incumbent's -2.9334. With an sd of 0.0034 per job and one run each, z = -0.0034 / (0.0034 * sqrt(2)) ≈ -0.707. The harness reports -0.714; the gap is probably because -2.93 is a rounded value. Rejecting is justified.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The diff reads no files, uses no network, pastes no coordinates and does not touch the harness. All new randomness comes from the seeded rng.

No bug that makes the result meaningless. _mixed_start only replaces the starting point. It draws radii log-uniformly in [0.02, 0.12], sorts them from largest to smallest and places each circle at the best of up to 20 random positions inside the square. The x0 vector has the same layout as before: 2n centre values, then n radii. SLSQP and the existing repair step still run afterwards, so validity is still enforced.
Small cleanup: INIT_LOW and INIT_RADIUS may no longer be used anywhere. If so, they are dead constants to remove under the simplicity rule.

Recomputed z: the difference is 2.9352 - 2.9334 = 0.0018. With one run on each side, the noise is 0.0034 * sqrt(2) = 0.0048, so z = 0.37. The harness value of 0.355 fits once you allow for the 4-decimal rounding of the shown values. Either way the result is well inside the noise, so 'reject' is the right provisional decision. With one run each, the test has little power. If you want to keep this idea, replicate it rather than accept it.
Both values are well above the starting script's mean of about 2.9253 and close to the published best of about 2.9370. Nothing in the numbers contradicts any claim.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. There is no file or network access and no pasted coordinates. Randomness still comes from the seed path, and the bound constraints are unchanged.

No bug that makes the result meaningless. Each pass drops far-apart pairs from the SLSQP constraints. Because of that, the result can come back with overlaps if the 3 passes run out before the all-pairs check passes. The repair step that comes after still makes the packing valid, so this costs quality, not validity.
Possible cost: up to 3 SLSQP solves per restart means fewer restarts fit in the time budget. That may explain the lower score.
Recomputed z = (2.9264 - 2.9334) / (0.0034 * sqrt(2)) = -1.456. This matches the reported -1.454; the difference comes from rounding. Negative means the candidate is worse.
There is only 1 run per side, so the evidence is weak. Still, the candidate is worse, and rejecting it is the right call.
